youtube_title: Why Chips Packets Are HALF Air 🥔 #Shorts
youtube_description:
That 'air' in a chips packet is mostly nitrogen. Oxygen makes the oil go stale and moisture makes chips soggy; nitrogen keeps them crisp, and the gas cushions them so they don't arrive as crumbs.

The hidden part: the extra space (called 'slack fill') also makes the packet LOOK like more food. Your eyes judge size, not grams.

Rule: ignore packet size, read the NET WEIGHT, compare price per gram.

Source: Mental Floss, 'Why are potato chip bags always half empty?'
